summary: OpenAI describes GPT-Red, an automated red-teaming model trained via self-play reinforcement learning to generate prompt-injection attacks, which it uses to adversarially train GPT-5.6 Sol and reports large reductions in prompt-injection failure rates.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI states it dedicated an unprecedented amount of compute, comparable to its largest post-training runs, specifically to train the red-teaming model for safety.
mechanisms.quote: We trained GPT‑Red at the compute scale of some of our largest post-training runs at OpenAI—an unprecedented amount of compute dedicated purely for improving safety.

practices.reason: Describes a concrete self-play red-teaming methodology with threat models and quantified attack success rates, but it is trained at extreme internal compute scale and kept internal-only, so it changes what to measure without directly handing over a reusable instrument.
practices.quote: GPT‑Red is trained using self-play reinforcement learning, where the model and a collection of diverse defender LLMs are trained simultaneously on a broad set of red-teaming scenarios.

practices.reason: GPT-5.6 Sol is reported as substantially more resistant to prompt injection attacks than the prior production model, an unreplicated lab-internal robustness measurement relevant to reliability-focused deployments.
practices.quote: GPT‑5.6 Sol is our most robust model to prompt injections to date, achieving 6x fewer failures on our hardest direct prompt injection benchmark compared to our best production model from just four months earlier.
